variables.user_request: Start a new prism-evaluate workflow. At present workflow-server workflows are slow and expensive to run. Many operations that are agent-driven can be mechanised. For example, if the user provides a named component, an issue or a PR, a TypeScript or Python script can extract the repo name and match it against a mono-repo component purely mechanically without agent interaction — saving a lot of time and tokens. There are no doubt many other opportunities to do this. I want a report detailing any and all opportunities for optimisation of the meta and work-package workflows. Use the example provided as a guide but do not limit the report to it.

data.name: evaluation_description
data.value: Find every opportunity to make the meta and work-package workflows faster and cheaper to run. The primary lead is mechanisation: agent-executed technique prose that is in fact a deterministic procedure a script or server tool could compute without agent involvement — the worked example is resolving a named component, issue or PR to a repository and matching it against a monorepo component, treated as a guide rather than a boundary. In scope as subject: workflows/meta/** and workflows/work-package/**. In scope as mechanisation surface: src/** and scripts/**. Deliverable is a report enumerating opportunities, each with the saving it buys and what it costs to build.

value.description: Which agent-executed steps are deterministic procedures a server tool or script could compute instead.
focus_areas: repo, component, issue and PR coordinate resolution
path derivation, repo-type and project-type detection
artifact link and anchor checking
planning README Progress-table synchronisation
git state inspection, branch and worktree verification
classification steps that are really fixed decision tables
format and schema validation of written artifacts
the 26 existing scripts/check-*.ts guards, reachable today only as repo CI and never as a workflow operation
value.name: Mechanisation Potential

value.description: Tokens spent shipping definition content into agent contexts, and where that delivery is redundant or oversized.
focus_areas: technique and resource body size against what a step actually reads
duplication between the meta and work-package trees
eager step-technique bundling budget behaviour
reference-versus-full delivery effectiveness and the agent_id ledger
inherited-input blocks restated per technique
resources fetched but never read
prose that restates what the schema already enforces
value.name: Context Economy

value.description: How work is distributed across agents and turns, and where the shape itself is the cost.
focus_areas: dispatch granularity and batch bounds
serial steps that could run concurrently
worker round trips to the server per activity
checkpoint placement and blocking gates — 44 checkpoint blocks across 13 work-package activities
context re-establishment at every activity boundary
sub-agent spawn overhead
value.name: Orchestration Topology

value.description: Work the workflows perform that produces nothing the run consumes.
focus_areas: steps duplicated across meta and work-package
activities and techniques never reached in practice
artifacts written but never read downstream
verification repeated at multiple stages
optional branches that always resolve the same way
value.name: Redundant Work

value.description: For each opportunity, what building it costs and what it risks.
focus_areas: implementation surface — new server tool versus script versus definition edit
existing guard and test coverage protecting the change
saved-session and backwards compatibility
whether the saving is measurable with the record_usage instrumentation already present
sequencing and dependencies between opportunities
value.name: Change Economics

data.name: scope_summary
data.value: Target /home/mike1/projects/dev/workflow-server, classified mixed. Subject: workflows/meta (5 activities, 150 techniques, 7 resources) and workflows/work-package (15 activities, 112 techniques, 37 resources). Mechanisation surface: src/ (712 KB TypeScript) and scripts/ (44 scripts, 26 check-* guards). Output to the session planning folder, verified writable. Five dimensions: Mechanisation Potential, Context Economy, Orchestration Topology, Redundant Work, Change Economics. Scoping-pass finding that shapes the dimensions: the server's entire tool surface is session control-plane with no domain-computation tool of any kind, so deterministic domain work in these workflows currently has nowhere to live except agent-executed prose. Confirmed by the user at the confirm-scope gate with option accept.
